newsitem.title: THAILAND: Little fallout seen from Thai minister quitting.
newsitem.headline: Little fallout seen from Thai minister quitting.

text.p: The sudden departure of the Thai finance minister added to the negative mood on the country's sagging bourse on Tuesday but should not have a major economic policy impact ahead of next month's election, analysts said.

They said Bodi Chunnananda's unexpected resignation on Monday was another blow to Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's lame-duck government, which has struggled for months to overcome economic problems.
Bodi, who was appointed finance minister in May, told Reuters on Tuesday he resigned to avoid conflict with other ministers, but would not elaborate.
He refused to comment on speculation that he quit over disagreement over proposed budget cuts and the timing of new banking licences.

The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) index, which has been on a downward spiral and is at a 39-month low, continued to drop in thin trade on Tuesday. It was down 1.96 percent at 900.33 points by mid-afternoon.

Analysts said Bodi's resignation was only a secondary factor to the market's decline. They said the selling was mainly due to negative outlook on the economy, expectations of poor third quarter earnings and uncertainty over the outcome of the November 17 election.

"It has minimal significance," said James Marshall, head of research for Nomura Securities, when asked about Bodi's resignation. "We didn't really expect Bodi to be particularly active in the next month."
Government officials said on Tuesday deputy finance minister Chaiyawat Wibulswadi would assume Bodi's duties and act as minister until the end of Banharn's administration.

But most analysts said Chaiyawat, who is a deputy central bank governor and was appointed to the deputy finance portfolio on September 27, was not likely to make major changes or policy moves during his month in office.

Bodi was the fourth senior finance official to leave Banharn's administration. In addition to Surakiart, former central banker Vijit Supinit and Securities and Exchange Commission head Ekamol Kiriwat were asked to step down over the past 14 months.
Marshall said Bodi probably left to distance himself from Banharn's Chart Thai party, which is not expected to fare well in the upcoming election.
